snapshot.title: Constitution — Parts, Articles, Schedules & Constituent Assembly
snapshot.exam_hook: 🏔️ UPSC Ranker Hook: B.N. Rau≠Drafting Committee. Nov 26: Constitution Day NOT Republic Day(Jan 26). Original articles: 395 NOT 448+. DPSP: Ireland NOT UK. 9th Schedule: 1st Amendment NOT 42nd.

quick_notes.title: Constitution Structure
quick_notes.detail: Original Constitution (1949): 22 Parts, 395 Articles, 8 Schedules. Current structure: 25 Parts, 448+ Articles, 12 Schedules, 5 Appendices. Common UPSC trap: "Originally how many articles?" = 395 NOT 448.

quick_notes.title: Constituent Assembly
quick_notes.detail: Formed: Cabinet Mission Plan 1946. First meeting: Dec 9, 1946. Adopted: Nov 26, 1949 (Constitution Day/Samvidhan Divas). Enforced: Jan 26, 1950 (Republic Day). Members who signed: 299. Time taken: 2 years, 11 months, 18 days. Constituent Assembly President: Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Constitutional Advisor: B.N. Rau (NOT Drafting Committee member).

quick_notes.title: Key Committees
quick_notes.detail: Drafting Committee: Ambedkar. Union Powers Committee: Nehru. Union Constitution Committee: Nehru. Provincial Constitution Committee: Patel. Advisory Committee on FRs: Patel. Rules & Procedure Committee: Rajendra Prasad. Exam trap: Ambedkar: Drafting ONLY. Patel: FRs+Provincial.

quick_notes.title: Sources of Constitution
quick_notes.detail: Parliamentary system+Rule of Law: UK. Fundamental Rights+Judicial Review: USA. DPSP: Ireland. Emergency provisions: Weimar Germany. Concurrent List+Joint Sitting: Australia. Fundamental Duties: USSR. Amendment procedure Art 368: South Africa. Five Year Plans: USSR. Federal with strong Centre: Canada.

quick_notes.title: Twelve Schedules
quick_notes.detail: 1st: States+UTs. 2nd: Salaries(President, Governors, Judges, CAG). 3rd: Oaths. 4th: Rajya Sabha seats allocation. 5th: Scheduled Areas. 6th: Tribal Areas(NE:Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram). 7th: Union(97)+State(61)+Concurrent(52) Lists [MOST TESTED]. 8th: 22 Official Languages. 9th: Acts protected from judicial review(added by 1st Amendment 1951). 10th: Anti-defection(52nd Amendment 1985). 11th: PR 29 subjects(73rd Amendment). 12th: ULB 18 subjects(74th Amendment).

snapshot.mastery_depth: Today you will learn the structure of the Indian Constitution, the original and current count of Parts, Articles and Schedules, the Constituent Assembly timeline, key committees, borrowed features, and all 12 Schedules. Focus especially on original vs current numbers, because that is a common UPSC trap.

topic_title: Constitution — Parts, Articles, Schedules & Constituent Assembly
lesson_intro: Before studying any individual topic in Indian Polity — Fundamental Rights, Parliament, the President — you need a mental map of the entire Constitution. Think of it like the table of contents of a massive book. The Constituent Assembly first met on December 9, 1946. By November 26, 1949, the Constitution was adopted. It came into force on January 26, 1950 — chosen to honour the 1930 Purna Swaraj declaration. The Constitution you study today is not what was adopted in 1949. The original had 395 Articles, 8 Schedules, and 22 Parts. Over 100+ amendments later: 448+ Articles, 12 Schedules, 25 Parts. UPSC tests both original and current numbers.
